declarations.name: repellingMultiplierOnePeriodEventualSupport_to_pointwiseAnalyticOrder
declarations.doc: Multiplier-one-period support data implies the older pointwise analytic-order input consumed by the existing connected q62 endpoints. The local bound only needs multiplier-one-period divisibility: when a fixed-point root is not multiplier-one it is simple, and when it is multiplier-one the supplied divisibility makes it a positive multiple of the exact multiplier-one return.

The `φ_{c₂}` transcendence input is produced internally from finite eventual support for multiplier-one roots, pointwise analytic-order bounds on that support, and eventual containment of non-strong roots. The remaining `c₁` datum is the native frontier separable nonresonant periodic fibre required by the hRigid branch.

declarations.name: multiplier_pow_analyticOrderAt_eq_character
declarations.doc: Equivariant analytic-order character law.** If a vector-valued analytic germ transforms by the character `χ` under an analytic self-map fixing `c`, then `χ` equals the self-map multiplier raised to the germ's vanishing order. The invariant multiplier and deck-character laws are the special case `χ = 1`.

exploration.name: eventually_analyticOrderAt_fixedPointPoly_eval_le_of_exact_period_returnOrder
exploration.doc: Exact-period form using analytic order of the first-return displacement instead of an explicit unit factor. This is usually the most convenient local parabolic input: once the return displacement has finite order `r ≥ 2`, the endpoint's eventual fixed-point-polynomial order bound follows.

exploration.name: multiplier_pow_analyticOrderAt_eq_one
exploration.doc: The multiplier law.** If an analytic map `τ` fixes `c` and `f ∘ τ = f` on a neighbourhood of `c`, then the multiplier `τ'(c)` is a `(ord_c f)`-th root of unity: `(τ'(c)) ^ ord_c f = 1`. Mechanism: peel `f = (·−c)^m · h` with `h c ≠ 0`; then near `c`, `f(τ s) = f s` reads `h s = (slope τ c s)^m · h(τ s)`, and the difference quotient `slope τ c s → τ'(c)` as `s → c`, so `h c = (τ'(c))^m · h c`, whence `(τ'(c))^m = 1`. No argument principle; the affine reflection lemma is the special case `τ s = 2c − s`, `τ'(c) = −1`.

exploration.name: analyticOrderAt_eq_of_factor_ne_zero
